transcript.text: AEG oven BPK556260M flashes F102 every time I try to start the pyro clean. Normal cooking seems ok. What's F102?

[Heading: Pyrolytic door lock mechanism fault]
On AEG ovens, F102 typically indicates a fault with the pyrolytic door lock system. Since normal cooking works fine, this isolates the issue to the safety mechanism that engages specifically for high-temperature self-cleaning. 1. 2. The pyrolytic door lock motor or latch assembly has failed.
3. Please ensure the door is firmly closed and check for any debris in the seal area. If the error persists with a properly closed door, the lock mechanism itself is likely faulty and will need replacement by an engineer.

Door's shut properly and the seal looks fine. I switched it off at the mains for a few minutes and retried, still F102. Is the lock a part I can buy myself, or should I call AEG? It's still in guarantee for another month.

[Heading: Pyrolytic door lock mechanism failure]
Because your oven is still under guarantee for another month, I strongly recommend calling AEG to arrange a repair. Attempting to replace this part yourself would likely void your warranty and involves working on high-voltage components inside the appliance, which should be left to qualified engineers.

claimsRejected.claim: The door is not fully latched or there is an obstruction in the seal preventing the lock from engaging.
A microswitch providing position feedback to the control board is faulty.

candidates.cause: Pyrolytic door lock mechanism fault (motor or latch)
Door not fully closed or obstruction in seal
Control PCB fault (less likely given normal cooking works)
